title: bug: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 the ps1 wrapper keeps '.', relative and in-project PATH entries, so its own bare `& git` and its worktree-launch and board-snapshot Node programs can run a project git.exe (ps1 twin of task-0b2ea570)
description:
Found while planning task-52555102 (prototype and logs in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/52555102-plan).

Measured on 2026-11-03 on this Windows host, with PS 5.1 and PS 7:
- With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 and a '.' entry first on PATH, a protected governor launch of moe-agent.ps1 runs a <project>\git.exe planted at the project root. The wrapper's own PowerShell `& git` calls run it, not the agent Git guard.
- PowerShell walks '.', relative and in-project PATH entries. Find-MoeProtectedFile skips them only for node and the agent CLI, and $env:PATH is left as inherited.

Two more wrapper Node programs spawn git by bare name with no cwd option:
- Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch's `git` helper: scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~:3260, sh twin prepare_worktree_launch ~:3394.
- Invoke-MoeBoardSnapshot: ~:7345, sh twin board_snapshot ~:7858.

On Node 22+ (libuv 1.48+), the NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 that task-2f22237b exports already stops the implicit current-directory lookup (mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first, re-measured 2026-11-03). Two gaps remain:
- libuv still walks '.', relative and in-project PATH entries.
- Node 20 and older ignore the variable.
task-0b2ea570 covers the sh wrapper's PATH and moe-call.sh; this row is the ps1 twin.

Fix direction:
- Under the marker, rewrite $env:PATH once, early (right after the marker is read and before any bare-name call), to the absolute entries outside the project that Find-MoeProtectedFile accepts.
- And/or pass task-52555102's trusted git path to the worktree-launch and board-snapshot programs. Keep both wrappers' program texts identical, as their twin tests require.
- Mirror whatever design task-0b2ea570 lands for sh.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 on Windows, a git.exe planted at the project root and reachable through a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry never runs during a protected governor launch of moe-agent.ps1. The check is the whole exe log, not only the agent Git guard's children. A protected-agent-command row run through Windows node.exe proves it for PS 5.1 and PS 7.
Under the marker, the worktree-launch and board-snapshot Node programs never spawn git by bare name, in either twin. A test row or a mutant-checked assertion pins this.
Legacy seats are unchanged. parity-check.sh, the protected-agent-command and agent-git-guard suites, and the launcher suites exit 0 on Linux and through Windows node.exe.

comments.content:
Planner note from architect-24611a0a, 2026-11-03.

This row now dependsOn task-89579137, which is planned at rev 1 and WORKING. Both rows touch scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs.

task-89579137 makes these changes:
- Moves Get-MoeSha256Hex up, above Find-MoeProtectedFile.
- Adds $script:MoeFinalPathDefinition and Get-MoeFinalPath. These use C# GetFinalPathNameByHandleW, compiled with Add-Type under a source-hash type name.
- On Windows, Find-MoeProtectedFile skips an entry whose final path is the project or lies under it. That covers 8.3, subst (including a subst rooted inside the project), \\?\ and junction spellings.
- It never trusts a network entry, meaning any entry whose final path starts with \\?\UNC\.
- It appends rows I1 and I2 at the end of the test file.

When you plan the ps1 PATH scrub, reuse that same entry test, so that the scrub and Find-MoeProtectedFile agree on what "outside the project" means. Append your rows after I2.

Evidence is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/89579137-plan/README.txt.
